_help: Day 1, room 4: the living room, 'Rainy days' (2003-2005). The fort rules work the lamp panel; the rainy-day number square's grey squares give the credenza code. See docs/STORY.md.

locks._why: The garden doors' key was in the credenza drawers.
hints: The garden is waiting outside, but the doors are locked.
The key from the credenza drawers opens the garden doors.
Select the brass key, then tap the garden doors.

locks._why: Night inside the fort: no sunshine (sun off). Not without the stars (star on). Shells glow when the stars do (shell on). The sea is never where the shells are (wave off).
hints: A fort needs the right light. Who made the rules?
The fort rules are about the lamp panel by the garden doors.
Sun off, shell on, star on, wave off.

locks._why: The small key from behind the lamp panel opens the bookshelf cabinet.
hints: A small key, a small door low down.
The small key fits the bookshelf cabinet.
Select the small key, then tap the bookshelf cabinet.

locks._why: A 4x4 number square: every row, column and 2x2 box has 1-4 once.
hints: Rainy days meant number squares. Finish it.
Every row, every column and every 2x2 box needs 1, 2, 3 and 4 once.

locks._why: The torn-out page slid under the rug, where only Chloé can wriggle.
hints: Something slid somewhere only a small dog can go.
Chloé can wriggle under the rug.
Tap Chloé, then tap the rug.

locks._why: The grey squares of the finished number square, read like a book (row by row): 3, 2, 1, 4. 'Pocket money' goes in the drawers.
hints: Pocket money had to live somewhere in this room.
The grey squares of the number square open the credenza drawers.
Read the grey squares row by row, like a book: 3, 2, 1, 4.
